svg.title: A Nested Cohort That Reconciles to Base Revenue
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-base-retained-buyer-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: A Nested Cohort That Reconciles to Base Revenue; subtitle: Annual retained purchases, not clicks multiplied across unrelated cohorts.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative annual cohort: every downstream group is a subset of the preceding group of distinct visitors. Each retained buyer places exactly one retained order averaging $75 in recognized sales after refunds, excluding collected sales tax. Repeat orders are excluded from this simplified model.; caption: 15,000 retained orders × $75 = $1,125,000 annual Base revenue. The modeled 3% visitor-to-retained-buyer conversion is an assumption to test, not a traffic benchmark.; stages: label: Eligible distinct visitors entering the storefront; value: 500,000 visitors in the annual starting cohort; numeric value: 500000.0; detail: Deduplicate measured visitors using an appropriate first-party analytics design. Keep acquisition spend separate from attribution claims and record measurement limits.; label: Visitors reaching an eligible product page; value: 200,000 visitors; 40% of the preceding cohort; numeric value: 200000.0; detail: Count only original-cohort visitors viewing stocked, purchasable products. Broken variant links and unavailable inventory should be diagnosed before increasing spend.; label: Product viewers adding an item to cart; value: 40,000 visitors; 20% of product-page viewers; numeric value: 40000.0; detail: Measure distinct cart creators rather than add-to-cart events. Investigate unexpected shipping charges and unclear product compatibility when this transition weakens.; label: Cart creators beginning the checkout sequence; value: 25,000 visitors; 62.5% of cart creators; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Restrict checkout starts to the same cart-creator cohort. Segment payment failures and address-validation friction without double-counting repeated checkout attempts.; label: Checkout starters retaining one completed purchase; value: 15,000 buyers; 60% of checkout starters; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Remove canceled and fully refunded purchases; use post-refund recognized order value for remaining buyers. This final cohort supplies exactly $1,125,000 annual sales.
